</div>
<div id="Thmlemma2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2</span></span><span id="Thmlemma2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Denoiser Formulation)<span id="Thmlemma2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The optimal autonomous target <math id="Thmlemma2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> can be expressed as an affine transformation of the optimal conditional denoiser <math id="Thmlemma2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{d(t)}{b(t)}\mathbf{u}+\left(c(t)-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\right)D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{d(t)}{b(t)}\mathbf{u}+\left(c(t)-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\right)D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A1.SS1.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Recall the unified forward process <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}=a(t)\mathbf{x}+b(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}=a(t)\mathbf{x}+b(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>. For a fixed observation <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> and noise level <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the noise <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> is deterministically related to the clean data <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> by:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\epsilon}=\frac{\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\epsilon}=\frac{\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Substitute this into the inner expectation of Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1 (Optimal Autonomous Target). ‣ A.1 Derivation of the Optimal Autonomous Target ‣ Appendix A General Derivations for Autonomous Models ‣ Appendices ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Note that conditioned on <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the terms <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)</annotation></semantics></math> are constants, leaving <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> as the only random variable:</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E26"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\E_{\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\epsilon}|\mathbf{u},t}[c(t)\mathbf{x}+d(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>𝔼</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\E_{\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\epsilon}|\mathbf{u},t}[c(t)\mathbf{x}+d(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E26.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\E_{\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t}\left[c(t)\mathbf{x}+d(t)\left(\frac{\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}\right)\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\E_{\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t}\left[c(t)\mathbf{x}+d(t)\left(\frac{\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}\right)\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E27"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E27.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=c(t)\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]+\frac{d(t)}{b(t)}\mathbf{u}-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=c(t)\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]+\frac{d(t)}{b(t)}\mathbf{u}-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">Identifying <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\E[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]</annotation></semantics></math> and grouping the coefficients for <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> yields the result.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Gradient of the Marginal Energy</h4>

<div id="Thmlemma3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3</span></span><span id="Thmlemma3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Gradient of the Marginal Energy)<span id="Thmlemma3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let the marginal likelihood be the mixture <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{u})=\int p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u})=\int p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt</annotation></semantics></math> and the marginal energy be <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=-\log p(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">marg</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=-\log p(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math>. The gradient of the marginal energy is the posterior expectation of the conditional energy gradients:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=\E_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[-\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">marg</mtext></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">𝔼</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=\E_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[-\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">By definition, <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=-\frac{\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u})}{p(\mathbf{u})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext>marg</mtext></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=-\frac{\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u})}{p(\mathbf{u})}</annotation></semantics></math>. We differentiate the mixture integral under the sign:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E29.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u})=\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\int p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt=\int\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mo>∫</mo><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u})=\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\int p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt=\int\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">We use the log-derivative trick <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u}|t)=p(\mathbf{u}|t)\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u}|t)=p(\mathbf{u}|t)\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)</annotation></semantics></math> to rewrite the integrand:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u})=\int p(\mathbf{u}|t)\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}p(\mathbf{u})=\int p(\mathbf{u}|t)\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)dt.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text">Dividing by <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> allows us to identify the posterior density <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})=\frac{p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)}{p(\mathbf{u})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})=\frac{p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)}{p(\mathbf{u})}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E31"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext>marg</mtext></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E31.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=-\int\frac{p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)}{p(\mathbf{u})}\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo>∫</mo></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=-\int\frac{p(\mathbf{u}|t)p(t)}{p(\mathbf{u})}\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)dt</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E32"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\int p(t|\mathbf{u})\left[-\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)\right]dt." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\int p(t|\mathbf{u})\left[-\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}\log p(\mathbf{u}|t)\right]dt.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Exact Analytical Forms for Autonomous Fields</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To facilitate the exact stability verification in Section <a href="#S6" title="6 Stability Conditions for Sampling with Autonomous Models ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Derivation of Stability Conditions ‣ Appendices ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>, we derive the closed-form expressions for the optimal autonomous vector fields. While the neural network approximates these expectations, we can compute them exactly when the data distribution <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{data}(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{data}(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math> is known.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">General Formulation.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall from Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2 (Denoiser Formulation). ‣ A.1 Derivation of the Optimal Autonomous Target ‣ Appendix A General Derivations for Autonomous Models ‣ Appendices ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> that the optimal autonomous field is an affine transformation of the posterior expectation of the conditional denoiser:</p>
<table id="A1.E33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{d(t)}{b(t)}\mathbf{u}+\left(c(t)-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\right)D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{d(t)}{b(t)}\mathbf{u}+\left(c(t)-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\right)D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The two key components required to evaluate this are:</p>
<ol id="A1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Optimal Conditional Denoiser</span> <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t]</annotation></semantics></math>. By Bayes’ rule, this is the center of mass of the posterior <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t)\propto p(\mathbf{u}|\mathbf{x},t)p_{data}(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{u},t)\propto p(\mathbf{u}|\mathbf{x},t)p_{data}(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Posterior Noise Distribution</span> <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math>. This allows us to average the conditional vector field over all possible noise levels.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Specialization to Discrete Data.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let the data manifold be a discrete set <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> with uniform prior <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x}_{k})=1/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x}_{k})=1/N</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">1. <span id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conditional Denoiser:</span> The likelihood of observing <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> given a specific source <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is Gaussian: <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{u}|\mathbf{x}_{k},t)=\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{u};a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k},b(t)^{2}I)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u}|\mathbf{x}_{k},t)=\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{u};a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k},b(t)^{2}I)</annotation></semantics></math>. The posterior probability <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{k}(\mathbf{u},t)\triangleq p(\mathbf{x}_{k}|\mathbf{u},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{k}(\mathbf{u},t)\triangleq p(\mathbf{x}_{k}|\mathbf{u},t)</annotation></semantics></math> is given by the softmax of the negative log-likelihoods:</p>
<table id="A1.E34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{k}(\mathbf{u},t)=\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}}{2b(t)^{2}}\right)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}_{j}\|^{2}}{2b(t)^{2}}\right)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{k}(\mathbf{u},t)=\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}}{2b(t)^{2}}\right)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}_{j}\|^{2}}{2b(t)^{2}}\right)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(34)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The optimal denoiser is the precision-weighted barycenter of the dataset:</p>
<table id="A1.E35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\sum_{k=1}^{N}w_{k}(\mathbf{u},t)\mathbf{x}_{k}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\sum_{k=1}^{N}w_{k}(\mathbf{u},t)\mathbf{x}_{k}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(35)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">2. <span id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Posterior Noise Distribution:</span> To compute the outer expectation <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[\cdot]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[\cdot]</annotation></semantics></math>, we require <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math>. The marginal likelihood <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{u}|t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u}|t)</annotation></semantics></math> is a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) with centers at <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Assuming a uniform prior on time <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t)\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t)\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, Bayes’ rule yields:</p>
<table id="A1.E36" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E36.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})=\frac{p(\mathbf{u}|t)}{\int_{0}^{1}p(\mathbf{u}|\tau)d\tau}\propto\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{u};a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k},b(t)^{2}I)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})=\frac{p(\mathbf{u}|t)}{\int_{0}^{1}p(\mathbf{u}|\tau)d\tau}\propto\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{u};a(t)\mathbf{x}_{k},b(t)^{2}I).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(36)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Therefore, for the case of discrete data prior, we can evaluate the unconditional field <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> by numerically integrating Eq. (<a href="#A1.E35" title="In Specialization to Discrete Data. ‣ A.3 Exact Analytical Forms for Autonomous Fields ‣ Appendix A General Derivations for Autonomous Models ‣ Appendices ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">35</span></a>) against this posterior <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> using high-precision quadrature on a dense grid <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[\epsilon,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[\epsilon,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. This eliminates sampling variance and allows us to isolate the geometric stability properties of the parameterization.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Concentration of <math id="A2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> via Proximity</h3>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide a rigorous proof that for autonomous generative models, the posterior distribution <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> converges weakly to a Dirac measure <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math> as the observation <math id="A2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> approaches the data support <math id="A2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We prove this result for two separate cases. In Case 1, we assume that the data is discrete and finite. In this case, we prove that if the ambient dimension satisfies <math id="A2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>, regardless of the number of data points, as we approach a data point the posterior <math id="A2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> converges weakly to the Dirac measure <math id="A2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>. In the second case, we assume that the data lies on a manifold, but the dimension of the manifold <math id="A2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and the ambient dimension <math id="A2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy <math id="A2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-d&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-d&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>. In this case, we show that as we approach the data manifold, the posterior <math id="A2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> again converges weakly to the Dirac measure <math id="A2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We first establish a general lemma for the concentration of the specific family of distributions that arise in our analysis.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4</span></span><span id="Thmlemma4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Concentration of the Inverse-Gamma Kernel)<span id="Thmlemma4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v;\beta)\propto v^{-\alpha}\exp(-\frac{\beta}{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mi>v</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v;\beta)\propto v^{-\alpha}\exp(-\frac{\beta}{v})</annotation></semantics></math> be a probability density on <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, with fixed shape <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math> and scale parameter <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. As the scale <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the distribution <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v;\beta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v;\beta)</annotation></semantics></math> converges weakly to a Dirac mass at zero: <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v;\beta)\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v;\beta)\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">This density is an Inverse-Gamma distribution <math id="A2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{IG}(\alpha-1,\beta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{IG}(\alpha-1,\beta)</annotation></semantics></math>. The mean and variance are given by <math id="A2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[v]=\frac{\beta}{\alpha-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[v]=\frac{\beta}{\alpha-2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Var}(v)=\frac{\beta^{2}}{(\alpha-2)^{2}(\alpha-3)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Var}(v)=\frac{\beta^{2}}{(\alpha-2)^{2}(\alpha-3)}</annotation></semantics></math> (for <math id="A2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math>).
As <math id="A2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, both the mean and the variance vanish. By Chebyshev’s inequality, the random variable <math id="A2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> converges in probability to 0, which implies weak convergence to <math id="A2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta(v)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Case 1: Discrete Data Support</h4>

<div id="Thmlemma5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5</span></span><span id="Thmlemma5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let the data support be a discrete set <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{x}_{j}+\boldsymbol{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>𝛅</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{x}_{j}+\boldsymbol{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\boldsymbol{\delta}\|=\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝛅</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\boldsymbol{\delta}\|=\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>. Assume the ambient dimension <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>, the prior <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous with <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(0)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(0)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and the noise schedule <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous, strictly increasing, with <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Then as <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v=b(t)^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v=b(t)^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> be the variance. Since <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly increasing and continuous with <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math>, the mapping <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\mapsto v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\mapsto v</annotation></semantics></math> is a homeomorphism near zero. Therefore, proving <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficient to imply <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">The marginal likelihood of the observation is a mixture of Gaussians:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E37.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{u}|v)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\underbrace{(2\pi v)^{-D/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}}{2v}\right)}_{L_{k}(v)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>v</mi><mo rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>exp</mi><mo>(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u}|v)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\underbrace{(2\pi v)^{-D/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}}{2v}\right)}_{L_{k}(v)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(37)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">By Bayes’ rule, the posterior <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> is a mixture of the individual component posteriors:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E38" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E38.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v|\mathbf{u})=\sum_{k=1}^{N}W_{k}(\epsilon)p_{k}(v|\mathbf{u})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v|\mathbf{u})=\sum_{k=1}^{N}W_{k}(\epsilon)p_{k}(v|\mathbf{u}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(38)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}(v|\mathbf{u})=\frac{L_{k}(v)p(v)}{Z_{k}(\epsilon)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}(v|\mathbf{u})=\frac{L_{k}(v)p(v)}{Z_{k}(\epsilon)}</annotation></semantics></math> is the normalized component posterior, and <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{k}(\epsilon)=\int_{0}^{\infty}L_{k}(z)p(z)dz" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{k}(\epsilon)=\int_{0}^{\infty}L_{k}(z)p(z)dz</annotation></semantics></math> is the component evidence. The mixing weights are determined by the ratio of component evidences: <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{k}(\epsilon)=\frac{Z_{k}(\epsilon)}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}Z_{i}(\epsilon)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{k}(\epsilon)=\frac{Z_{k}(\epsilon)}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}Z_{i}(\epsilon)}</annotation></semantics></math>.
