Note that since <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded below near zero, the induced prior <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v)\geq c_{0}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v)\geq c_{0}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> in a neighborhood of <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">We analyze the asymptotic behavior of the evidence integrals as <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. For the nearest neighbor (<math id="A2.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=j</annotation></semantics></math>), the squared distance is <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{j}\|^{2}=\epsilon^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{j}\|^{2}=\epsilon^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The evidence integral is:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E39.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Z_{j}(\epsilon)=\int_{0}^{\infty}(2\pi z)^{-D/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2z}\right)p(z)dz." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>z</mi><mo rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{j}(\epsilon)=\int_{0}^{\infty}(2\pi z)^{-D/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2z}\right)p(z)dz.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(39)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Substituting <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2z}</annotation></semantics></math> yields <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{j}(\epsilon)\propto(\epsilon^{2})^{1-D/2}\int_{0}^{\infty}y^{D/2-2}e^{-y}p(\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2y})dy" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{j}(\epsilon)\propto(\epsilon^{2})^{1-D/2}\int_{0}^{\infty}y^{D/2-2}e^{-y}p(\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2y})dy</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>, the integral converges to a finite value bounded away from zero. Consequently, the evidence scales as <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{j}(\epsilon)=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2-D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{j}(\epsilon)=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{2-D})</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2-D&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2-D&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{j}(\epsilon)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{j}(\epsilon)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">In contrast, for any other point <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\neq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\neq j</annotation></semantics></math>, the distance <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}\to\Delta_{jk}^{2}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}\to\Delta_{jk}^{2}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. The evidence integral <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{k}(\epsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{k}(\epsilon)</annotation></semantics></math> converges to a finite constant <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{k}(0)&lt;\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{k}(0)&lt;\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, as the exponential term <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\exp(-\Delta_{jk}^{2}/2z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\exp(-\Delta_{jk}^{2}/2z)</annotation></semantics></math> suppresses the singularity at <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">This divergence of the nearest-neighbor evidence implies that the mixing weights collapse:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E40" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E40.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{j}(\epsilon)=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{k\neq j}\frac{Z_{k}(\epsilon)}{Z_{j}(\epsilon)}}\to 1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{j}(\epsilon)=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{k\neq j}\frac{Z_{k}(\epsilon)}{Z_{j}(\epsilon)}}\to 1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(40)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">Thus, the posterior is asymptotically dominated by the nearest neighbor component <math id="A2.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{j}(v|\mathbf{u})\propto v^{-D/2}\exp(-\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2v})p(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{j}(v|\mathbf{u})\propto v^{-D/2}\exp(-\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2v})p(v)</annotation></semantics></math>. This is an Inverse-Gamma kernel with scale parameter <math id="A2.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=\epsilon^{2}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=\epsilon^{2}/2</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="A2.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the scale vanishes, and by Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma4" title="Lemma 4 (Concentration of the Inverse-Gamma Kernel). ‣ Appendix B Concentration of 𝑝(𝑡|𝐮) via Proximity ‣ Appendices ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, <math id="A2.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Case 2: Continuous Low-Dimensional Manifold</h4>

<div id="Thmlemma6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 6</span></span><span id="Thmlemma6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let data lie on a smooth (<math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional submanifold <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math> with codimension <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=D-d&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=D-d&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\text{dist}(\mathbf{u},\mathcal{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">dist</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\text{dist}(\mathbf{u},\mathcal{M})</annotation></semantics></math> be the orthogonal distance. Assume <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{data}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{data}</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous and bounded on <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">We analyze the marginal likelihood integral over the manifold <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of the variance <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v=b(t)^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v=b(t)^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E41" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E41.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p(\mathbf{u}|v)=\int_{\mathcal{M}}(2\pi v)^{-D/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}}{2v}\right)p_{data}(\mathbf{x})d\mathbf{x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msub><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>v</mi><mo rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u}|v)=\int_{\mathcal{M}}(2\pi v)^{-D/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}}{2v}\right)p_{data}(\mathbf{x})d\mathbf{x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(41)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{proj}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{proj}</annotation></semantics></math> be the orthogonal projection of the fixed observation <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> onto <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed, <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{proj}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{proj}</annotation></semantics></math> is a constant vector.
We define local coordinates on the manifold centered at <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{proj}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{proj}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> represent coordinates in the tangent space <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathbf{x}_{proj}}\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathbf{x}_{proj}}\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. For points <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> near <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{proj}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{proj}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have the expansion <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}(\mathbf{y})=\mathbf{x}_{proj}+\mathbf{J}\mathbf{y}+O(\|\mathbf{y}\|^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐉𝐲</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}(\mathbf{y})=\mathbf{x}_{proj}+\mathbf{J}\mathbf{y}+O(\|\mathbf{y}\|^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The squared distance decomposes as:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E42" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E42.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{proj}+\mathbf{x}_{proj}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=r^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}_{proj}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}\approx r^{2}+\|\mathbf{y}\|^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{proj}+\mathbf{x}_{proj}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=r^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}_{proj}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}\approx r^{2}+\|\mathbf{y}\|^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(42)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text">(The cross-term vanishes because <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{proj}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}_{proj}</annotation></semantics></math> is orthogonal to the tangent space).</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Substituting this into the integral:</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">We apply the Laplace method for asymptotic integrals as <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> (which corresponds to the high-likelihood regime). The Gaussian kernel <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="e^{-\|\mathbf{y}\|^{2}/2v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">−</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em">/</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>v</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-\|\mathbf{y}\|^{2}/2v}</annotation></semantics></math> concentrates mass entirely at <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}=0</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x}_{proj}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x}_{proj}</annotation></semantics></math>). Since <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{data}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{data}</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous, we can pull the value <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{data}(\mathbf{x}_{proj})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{data}(\mathbf{x}_{proj})</annotation></semantics></math> out of the integral:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A2.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">The remaining integral is a standard unnormalized Gaussian integral over <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> dimensions, equal to <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2\pi v)^{d/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\pi v)^{d/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Combining the pre-factors:</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=D-d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=D-d</annotation></semantics></math> be the codimension. The likelihood takes the form of an Inverse-Gamma kernel:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E46.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p(\mathbf{u}|v)\propto v^{-k/2}\exp\left(-\frac{r^{2}}{2v}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{u}|v)\propto v^{-k/2}\exp\left(-\frac{r^{2}}{2v}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(46)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text">Assuming a flat prior on <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> near 0 (or bounded <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v)</annotation></semantics></math>), the posterior <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> is an Inverse-Gamma distribution <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{IG}(\alpha,\beta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{IG}(\alpha,\beta)</annotation></semantics></math> with shape <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=\frac{k}{2}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=\frac{k}{2}-1</annotation></semantics></math> and scale <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=\frac{r^{2}}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=\frac{r^{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Provided <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>, the shape parameter <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. As the distance to the manifold <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the scale parameter <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. By Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma4" title="Lemma 4 (Concentration of the Inverse-Gamma Kernel). ‣ Appendix B Concentration of 𝑝(𝑡|𝐮) via Proximity ‣ Appendices ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, the distribution converges weakly to a Dirac mass: <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(v|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(v|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(v)</annotation></semantics></math>. This implies <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑤</mo></mover><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(t|\mathbf{u})\xrightarrow{w}\delta(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Posterior Concentration in High Dimensions</h3>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we prove that in high dimensions, the posterior distribution of the noise level concentrates sharply, effectively allowing noise-blind models to recover the time signal from the spatial geometry of the observation <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 1</span></span><span id="Thmproposition1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{V}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝕍</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{V}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math> be a linear subspace of dimension <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d&lt;D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d&lt;D</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐧</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{n}</annotation></semantics></math> be an observation where <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝕍</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{V}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{n}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}I_{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐧</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>D</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{n}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}I_{D})</annotation></semantics></math>. Assuming an improper flat prior <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x})\propto 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x})\propto 1</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, the posterior distribution <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\sigma|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\sigma|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> concentrates at <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}=\frac{r}{\sqrt{D-d}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>r</mi><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}=\frac{r}{\sqrt{D-d}}</annotation></semantics></math> with variance <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(D^{-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(D^{-1})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\min_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{V}}\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{y}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝕍</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐲</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\min_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{V}}\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{y}\|</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}^{*}=\text{proj}_{\mathbb{V}}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><mi>𝕍</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}^{*}=\text{proj}_{\mathbb{V}}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> be the orthogonal projection of <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> onto <math id="A3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{V}</annotation></semantics></math>. For any <math id="A3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝕍</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Pythagorean theorem yields the exact decomposition:</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}^{*}\|^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}^{*}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=r^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}^{*}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}^{*}\|^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}^{*}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}=r^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}^{*}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The marginal likelihood (or integrated likelihood) is defined as:</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle p(\mathbf{u}|\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle p(\mathbf{u}|\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{V}}p(\mathbf{u}|\mathbf{x},\sigma)p(\mathbf{x})\,d\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>𝕍</mi></msub></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{V}}p(\mathbf{u}|\mathbf{x},\sigma)p(\mathbf{x})\,d\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A3.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{D/2}}\int_{\mathbb{V}}\exp\left(-\frac{r^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}^{*}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,d\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>𝕍</mi></msub></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{D/2}}\int_{\mathbb{V}}\exp\left(-\frac{r^{2}+\|\mathbf{x}^{*}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,d\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">By defining an isometric isomorphism between <math id="A3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{V}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, we evaluate the integral over the subspace:</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle p(\mathbf{u}|\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle p(\mathbf{u}|\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\exp(-r^{2}/2\sigma^{2})}{(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{D/2}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{z}\|^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,d\mathbf{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>σ</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msub><mo>∫</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></msub></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>𝐳</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\exp(-r^{2}/2\sigma^{2})}{(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{D/2}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{z}\|^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,d\mathbf{z}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">The log-marginal likelihood <math id="A3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(\sigma)=\ln p(\mathbf{u}|\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(\sigma)=\ln p(\mathbf{u}|\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is:</span></p>

<p id="A3.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Solving <math id="A3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell^{\prime}(\sigma)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell^{\prime}(\sigma)=0</annotation></semantics></math> gives the maximum likelihood estimator:</span></p>

</div>
<div id="A3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">The observed Fisher Information <math id="A3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(\hat{\sigma})=-\ell^{\prime\prime}(\hat{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>′′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(\hat{\sigma})=-\ell^{\prime\prime}(\hat{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated at <math id="A3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> is:</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(\hat{\sigma})=\left[-\frac{D-d}{\sigma^{2}}+\frac{3r^{2}}{\sigma^{4}}\right]_{\sigma=\hat{\sigma}}=\frac{2(D-d)}{\hat{\sigma}^{2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(\hat{\sigma})=\left[-\frac{D-d}{\sigma^{2}}+\frac{3r^{2}}{\sigma^{4}}\right]_{\sigma=\hat{\sigma}}=\frac{2(D-d)}{\hat{\sigma}^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">As <math id="A3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> (with <math id="A3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> fixed), the posterior variance <math id="A3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Var}(\sigma|\mathbf{u})\approx\mathcal{I}(\hat{\sigma})^{-1}\propto(D-d)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Var}(\sigma|\mathbf{u})\approx\mathcal{I}(\hat{\sigma})^{-1}\propto(D-d)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes via the Laplace approximation. Furthermore, since <math id="A3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{2}/\sigma_{0}^{2}\sim\chi^{2}_{D-d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>∼</mo><msubsup><mi>χ</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{2}/\sigma_{0}^{2}\sim\chi^{2}_{D-d}</annotation></semantics></math>, the estimator <math id="A3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies <math id="A3.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\hat{\sigma}^{2}]=\sigma_{0}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\hat{\sigma}^{2}]=\sigma_{0}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Var}(\hat{\sigma}^{2})=\frac{2\sigma_{0}^{4}}{D-d}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup></mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Var}(\hat{\sigma}^{2})=\frac{2\sigma_{0}^{4}}{D-d}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. By the Continuous Mapping Theorem, <math id="A3.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> is a consistent estimator of the true noise level <math id="A3.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the posterior distribution <math id="A3.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\sigma|\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\sigma|\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> concentrates at the true value <math id="A3.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Derivation of General Energy-Aligned Decomposition</h3>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we derive the exact relationship between the learned autonomous vector field <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> and the gradient of the marginal energy <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext>marg</mtext></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> for general affine noise schedules.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recall the general autonomous form derived in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E7" title="In 3 Preliminaries: A Unified Schedule Formulation ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>):</p>
<table id="A4.E47" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{b(t)^{2}}{a(t)}\left(c(t)-\frac{d(t)a(t)}{b(t)}\right)=-\frac{b(t)^{2}c(t)}{a(t)}+b(t)d(t)=\frac{b(t)}{a(t)}\left(d(t)a(t)-c(t)b(t)\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(53)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Let us define this effective gradient gain as <math id="A4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(t)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E54" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E54.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(t)\triangleq\frac{b(t)}{a(t)}\left(d(t)a(t)-c(t)b(t)\right)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(t)\triangleq\frac{b(t)}{a(t)}\left(d(t)a(t)-c(t)b(t)\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(54)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p4.3" class="ltx_p">The autonomous field can now be written as:</p>
<table id="A4.E55" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E55.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\lambda(t)\nabla E_{t}(\mathbf{u})\right]+\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{c(t)}{a(t)}\right]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\lambda(t)\nabla E_{t}(\mathbf{u})\right]+\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{c(t)}{a(t)}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(55)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p4.4" class="ltx_p">Finally, we apply the covariance decomposition to the expectation term. Recall that the marginal energy gradient is the average of the conditional gradients: <math id="A4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[\nabla E_{t}(\mathbf{u})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext>marg</mtext></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[\nabla E_{t}(\mathbf{u})]</annotation></semantics></math>. Using the identity <math id="A4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[XY]=\mathbb{E}[X]\mathbb{E}[Y]+Cov(X,Y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[XY]=\mathbb{E}[X]\mathbb{E}[Y]+Cov(X,Y)</annotation></semantics></math>, we derive the <span id="A4.p4.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">General Energy-Aligned Decomposition</span>:</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A4.E56" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E56.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\underbrace{\overline{\lambda}(u)\nabla E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})}_{\text{Natural stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>E</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>marg</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Natural Gradient</mtext></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em"
