stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Transport Correction</mtext></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Linear Drift</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=\underbrace{\overline{\lambda}(u)\nabla E_{\text{marg}}(\mathbf{u})}_{\text{Natural Gradient}}+\underbrace{Cov(\lambda(t),\nabla E_{t}(\mathbf{u}))}_{\text{Transport Correction}}+\underbrace{\overline{c}_{scale}(\mathbf{u})\mathbf{u}}_{\text{Linear Drift}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(56)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\lambda}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[\lambda(t)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[\lambda(t)]</annotation></semantics></math> is the posterior effective gain, and <math id="A4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{c}_{scale}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[c(t)/a(t)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{c}_{scale}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbb{E}_{t|\mathbf{u}}[c(t)/a(t)]</annotation></semantics></math> is the mean linear drift coefficient. This result proves that for any affine schedule, the learned field is a sum of the marginal energy gradient (scaled by posterior uncertainty), a covariance correction term, and a linear drift.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Analysis of Specific Architectures: Exact Low-Noise Asymptotics</h3>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we show that near the data manifold, the effective gain <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\lambda}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> in the vector field vanishes at a rate that perfectly counteracts the divergence of the gradient of the marginal energy. We assume discrete data to analyze the asymptotic behavior of the learned autonomous field <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> near the data manifold (<math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}\to\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}\to\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>). We derive the exact form using the limit of the marginal energy gradient:</p>
<table id="A5.E57" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E57.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{marg}(\mathbf{u})\approx\frac{\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}}{b(t)^{2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></msub><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}E_{marg}(\mathbf{u})\approx\frac{\mathbf{u}-a(t)\mathbf{x}}{b(t)^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(57)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Substituting this into the General Energy-Aligned Decomposition (<math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f^{*}=\overline{\lambda}\nabla E+\text{Drift}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>+</mo><mtext>Drift</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}=\overline{\lambda}\nabla E+\text{Drift}</annotation></semantics></math>), we examine the properties of the target learned by each parameterization.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. DDPM and EDM (Noise/Data Prediction)</span>
For these models, <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(t)\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(t)\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math>. The effective gain is <math id="A5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(t)\approx b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(t)\approx b(t)</annotation></semantics></math> and the drift is zero.</p>
<table id="A5.E58" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E58.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\approx\underbrace{b(t)}_{\text{Gain}}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)^{2}}}_{\text{Gradient}}=\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}\sim O(1)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Gain</mtext></munder><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Gradient</mtext></munder></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\approx\underbrace{b(t)}_{\text{Gain}}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)^{2}}}_{\text{Gradient}}=\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}\sim O(1)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(58)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Result (Bounded Target):</span> The learned target (which corresponds to <math id="A5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> or scaled data) contains a removable singularity of order <math id="A5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1)</annotation></semantics></math>. While the target itself is bounded, it does not inherently define the flow dynamics. Standard diffusion ODEs typically scale this target by <math id="A5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/b(t)</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., <math id="A5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\mathbf{u}/dt\propto f^{*}/b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\mathbf{u}/dt\propto f^{*}/b(t)</annotation></semantics></math>). Thus, while the network learns a stable quantity, the implied autonomous dynamics may still diverge without careful parameterization (see Section 6).</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Flow Matching (Velocity Prediction)</span>
For Flow Matching, <math id="A5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(t)\approx 1-t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(t)\approx 1-t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)\approx t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)\approx t</annotation></semantics></math>. The gain is <math id="A5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(t)\approx t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(t)\approx t</annotation></semantics></math> and drift is <math id="A5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx-\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx-\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<table id="A5.E59" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E59.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\approx\underbrace{t}_{\text{Gain}}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\mathbf{u}-(1-t)\mathbf{x}}{t^{2}}}_{\text{Gradient}}\underbrace{-\mathbf{x}}_{\text{Drift}}=\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{t}\sim O(1)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Gain</mtext></munder><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Gradient</mtext></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Drift</mtext></munder></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\approx\underbrace{t}_{\text{Gain}}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\mathbf{u}-(1-t)\mathbf{x}}{t^{2}}}_{\text{Gradient}}\underbrace{-\mathbf{x}}_{\text{Drift}}=\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{t}\sim O(1)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(59)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Result (Stable Transport):</span> The learned target simplifies to a finite velocity vector. Crucially, for Flow Matching, this target <span id="A5.p3.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is</span> the ODE velocity (<math id="A5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\mathbf{u}/dt=f^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\mathbf{u}/dt=f^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math>). Since the target is <math id="A5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the resulting generation trajectories approach the manifold with finite speed, ensuring stable transport without numerical explosion.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3. Equilibrium Matching (Stabilized Transport)</span>
For EqM, the gain is higher-order <math id="A5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(t)\approx t^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(t)\approx t^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the drift coefficient vanishes.</p>
<table id="A5.E60" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E60.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\approx\underbrace{t^{2}}_{\text{Gain}}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\mathbf{u}-(1-t)\mathbf{x}}{t^{2}}}_{\text{Gradient}}+0=\mathbf{u}-(1-t)\mathbf{x}\xrightarrow{t\to 0}\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Gain</mtext></munder><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Gradient</mtext></munder></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">t</mi><mo mathsize="0.700em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mrow></mover><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\approx\underbrace{t^{2}}_{\text{Gain}}\cdot\underbrace{\frac{\mathbf{u}-(1-t)\mathbf{x}}{t^{2}}}_{\text{Gradient}}+0=\mathbf{u}-(1-t)\mathbf{x}\xrightarrow{t\to 0}\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(60)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Result (Vanishing Equilibrium):</span> The learned target scales with the distance to the manifold, vanishing as <math id="A5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|)</annotation></semantics></math>. Since EqM uses this target directly as the ODE velocity, the dynamics naturally slow down and stop at the data (<math id="A5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\mathbf{u}/dt\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\mathbf{u}/dt\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>). This creates a stable fixed point at the manifold, contrasting with the constant-velocity transport of Flow Matching.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Derivation of Stability Conditions</h3>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this appendix, we provide the derivation of the Unified Sampler Dynamics and the rigorous proofs for the stability limits of the three parameterizations discussed in Section <a href="#S6" title="6 Stability Conditions for Sampling with Autonomous Models ‣ The Geometry of Noise: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Need Noise Conditioning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Unified Sampler Dynamics</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For general affine noise schedules defined by <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{t}=a(t)\mathbf{x}+b(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{t}=a(t)\mathbf{x}+b(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>, the generation process involves integrating a differential equation. We derive the exact ODE by inverting the linear system relating the data, noise, and observation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The flow of the process is given by differentiating the forward process:</p>
<table id="A6.E61" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E61.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{\mathbf{u}}=\dot{a}(t)\mathbf{x}+\dot{b}(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{\mathbf{u}}=\dot{a}(t)\mathbf{x}+\dot{b}(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(61)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">An autonomous generative model predicts a target <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=c(t)\mathbf{x}+d(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})=c(t)\mathbf{x}+d(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>. Combining this with the observation identity <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}=a(t)\mathbf{x}+b(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}=a(t)\mathbf{x}+b(t)\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>, we form the linear system:</p>
<table id="A6.E62" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E62.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{u}\\
f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}a(t)&amp;b(t)\\
c(t)&amp;d(t)\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}\\
\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\end{bmatrix}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>𝐮</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>𝐱</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{u}\\
f^{*}(\mathbf{u})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}a(t)&amp;b(t)\\
c(t)&amp;d(t)\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}\\
\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\end{bmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(62)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Solving for <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> and substituting them into the flow equation <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{\mathbf{u}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{\mathbf{u}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain the general sampler ODE:</p>
<table id="A6.E63" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E63.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{d\mathbf{u}}{dt}=\underbrace{\left(\frac{\dot{a}d-\dot{b}c}{ad-bc}\right)}_{\mu(t)}\mathbf{u}+\underbrace{\left(\frac{\dot{b}a-\dot{a}b}{ad-bc}\right)}_{\nu(t)}f^{*}(\mathbf{u})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d\mathbf{u}}{dt}=\underbrace{\left(\frac{\dot{a}d-\dot{b}c}{ad-bc}\right)}_{\mu(t)}\mathbf{u}+\underbrace{\left(\frac{\dot{b}a-\dot{a}b}{ad-bc}\right)}_{\nu(t)}f^{*}(\mathbf{u}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(63)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">We identify <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(t)</annotation></semantics></math> as the schedule drift coefficient and <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu(t)</annotation></semantics></math> as the effective gain of the parameterization.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In order to analyze the stability of generation, we also consider generation using the optimal conditional model <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}_{t}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}_{t}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> that has access to the noise level. We define the Drift Perturbation Error <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐯</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}</annotation></semantics></math> as the norm difference between the autonomous drift (using <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math>) and the oracle drift. Since the linear term <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(t)\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(t)\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> is identical for both, it cancels out giving us:</p>
<table id="A6.E64" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E64.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{u},t)=|\nu(t)|\cdot\|f^{*}(\mathbf{u})-f_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐯</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{u},t)=|\nu(t)|\cdot\|f^{*}(\mathbf{u})-f_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(64)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">If this Drift Perturbation Error has singularities in it, this results in unstable generation dynamics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Stability Analysis by Parameterization</h4>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the limit of <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐯</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> (near the data manifold) for standard models. We assume standard boundary conditions <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(t)\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(t)\to 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Case 1: Noise Prediction (DDPM/DDIM)</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Target: <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=0,d=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=0,d=1</annotation></semantics></math>).
The effective gain simplifies to <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu(t)=\frac{\dot{b}a-\dot{a}b}{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>a</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu(t)=\frac{\dot{b}a-\dot{a}b}{a}</annotation></semantics></math>. Near the manifold (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\approx 1,\dot{a}\approx 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\approx 1,\dot{a}\approx 0</annotation></semantics></math>), the gain behaves as the noise derivative: <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu(t)\approx\dot{b}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu(t)\approx\dot{b}(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The optimal conditional target near the manifold is given by the geometric relation <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}_{t}(\mathbf{u})\approx\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}_{t}(\mathbf{u})\approx\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Substituting this into the error norm:</p>
<table id="A6.E65" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E65.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{noise}\approx\dot{b}(t)\left\|\mathbb{E}_{\tau|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(\tau)}\right]-\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}\right\|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{noise}\approx\dot{b}(t)\left\|\mathbb{E}_{\tau|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(\tau)}\right]-\frac{\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}}{b(t)}\right\|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(65)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Factoring out the geometric direction <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|</annotation></semantics></math>, we isolate the scaling behavior:</p>
<table id="A6.E66" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E66.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{noise}\approx\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|\left|\frac{\dot{b}(t)}{b(t)}\underbrace{\left(b(t)\mathbb{E}_{\tau|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{1}{b(\tau)}\right]-1\right)}_{\text{Jensen Gap}}\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Jensen Gap</mtext></munder></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{noise}\approx\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{x}\|\left|\frac{\dot{b}(t)}{b(t)}\underbrace{\left(b(t)\mathbb{E}_{\tau|\mathbf{u}}\left[\frac{1}{b(\tau)}\right]-1\right)}_{\text{Jensen Gap}}\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(66)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">We call the term in the parenthesis the “Jensen Gap”, the difference between the harmonic mean of noise levels and the true noise level, which converges to a non-zero constant due to the strict convexity of <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/x</annotation></semantics></math> unless the posterior <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p({\tau|\mathbf{u}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p({\tau|\mathbf{u}})</annotation></semantics></math> converges to a Dirac measure <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta(\tau-t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta(\tau-t)</annotation></semantics></math>. The instability is driven by the pre-factor <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\dot{b}(t)}{b(t)}=\frac{d}{dt}\ln b(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\dot{b}(t)}{b(t)}=\frac{d}{dt}\ln b(t)</annotation></semantics></math>. For any polynomial noise schedule <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)\propto t^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)\propto t^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> (where <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>), this term diverges as <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1/t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1/t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consequently, <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{t\to 0}\Delta\mathbf{v}_{noise}=\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{t\to 0}\Delta\mathbf{v}_{noise}=\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, rendering the dynamics structurally unstable for autonomous noise prediction. Note that for Variance Preserving SDEs where <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)\propto\sqrt{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msqrt><mi>t</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)\propto\sqrt{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the singularity is even stronger (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t^{-1.5})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(t^{-1.5})</annotation></semantics></math>), but the divergence exists even for linear schedules (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(t)=t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(t)=t</annotation></semantics></math>) that is used in flow matching.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Case 2: Signal Prediction (EDM)</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Target: <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=1,d=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=1,d=0</annotation></semantics></math>).
The effective gain scales as <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu(t)\approx\frac{1}{b(t)^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu(t)\approx\frac{1}{b(t)^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The drift error is determined by the denoising error:</p>
<table id="A6.E67" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E67.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{signal}\approx\frac{1}{b(t)^{2}}\|\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{u})-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{signal}\approx\frac{1}{b(t)^{2}}\|\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{u})-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})\|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(67)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">To resolve the <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0/0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0/0</annotation></semantics></math> indeterminacy, we assume the data manifold is discrete, <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>. Near a specific data point <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, the optimal conditional denoiser <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> is a softmax-weighted average of the dataset. The error is dominated by the distance to the nearest neighbor <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, with a weight proportional to the Gaussian likelihood ratio:</p>
<table id="A6.E68" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E68.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{x}_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|\propto\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{x}_{j}-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}}{2b(t)^{2}}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{x}_{t}^{*}(\mathbf{u})-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|\propto\exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{x}_{j}-\mathbf{x}_{k}\|^{2}}{2b(t)^{2}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(68)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">This error decays <span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">exponentially</span> with respect to the inverse variance <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/b(t)^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/b(t)^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since the noise-agnostic estimator <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{u})</annotation></semantics></math> is a mixture of these conditional estimators, it inherits this exponential decay.
The limit becomes a competition between the polynomial divergence of the gain and the exponential convergence of the estimator:</p>
<table id="A6.E69" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E69.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{e^{-C/b(t)^{2}}}{b(t)^{2}}=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{e^{-C/b(t)^{2}}}{b(t)^{2}}=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(69)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Thus, <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{t\to 0}\Delta\mathbf{v}_{signal}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{t\to 0}\Delta\mathbf{v}_{signal}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, proving that signal prediction is asymptotically stable for autonomous models on discrete data manifolds.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Case 3: Velocity Prediction (Flow Matching)</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Target: <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}=\dot{\mathbf{u}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}=\dot{\mathbf{u}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=-1,d=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=-1,d=1</annotation></semantics></math>).
The denominator of the unified coefficients is <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ad-bc=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ad-bc=1</annotation></semantics></math>, resulting in a constant gain <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu(t)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu(t)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The error norm is simply the posterior deviation of the velocity field:</p>
<table id="A6.E70" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E70.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{FM}=\|\mathbb{E}_{\tau|\mathbf{u}}[f^{*}_{\tau}(\mathbf{u})]-f^{*}_{t}(\mathbf{u})\|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>𝐮</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>τ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{FM}=\|\mathbb{E}_{\tau|\mathbf{u}}[f^{*}_{\tau}(\mathbf{u})]-f^{*}_{t}(\mathbf{u})\|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(70)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Since the optimal autonomous targets <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> are bounded and the gain <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is unity, the error term does not contain singularities. Therefore, the Drift Perturbation Error <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{FM}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{FM}</annotation></semantics></math> remains bounded, indicating that velocity parameterization is inherently stable for autonomous generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
</section>
</article>
</div>
</div>
